articles.title: Mckenna Grace Says Refusal to Do Nudity on Camera Is ‘Unrelated’ to Her Disney Princess Dreams
articles.summary: "Silly that it’s become such a source of conversation," the "Sunrise on the Reaping" actress says of her viral Cosmopolitan interview.
articles.body:
Mckenna Grace appeared to take issue with her viral interview in Cosmopolitan on Tuesday, clarifying on Instagram that her quote about dreaming of being a Disney princess and refusing to do on-camera nudity are "unrelated."

"The two quotes being used right now in these titles are unrelated," the "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" star wrote in an Instagram story alongside a screenshot of Variety's coverage of the Cosmo conversation. (The publication's headline, "Mckenna Grace Rejects 'Nudity or Hypersexual Things' in Acting Roles Because 'My Dream Is to Be a Disney Princess Someday,' was what the actress took issue with.)

"I said at this point in my career I think I'm uncomfortable doing something but I respect everyone who does — and I also have a dream job!" Grace continued. "I'm not uncomfortable doing nude scenes/hypersexual roles simply because 'I want to be a Disney princess,' it's just because of my own personal comfortability I have with that sort of thing right now at this point in my life!"

The 20-year-old actress, who got her start as a child and teen star in projects like "Designated Survivor," "I, Tonya" and "The Haunting of Hill House," emphasized that it's "silly that it's become such a source of conversation! So many more important things to talk about."

The pushback came about Tuesday after outlets like Variety , Deadline and People published stories on her boundaries with nudity as if it had to do with her future aspirations of being a Disney princess. The original quote in full was:

"At this point, I definitely don't do nudity or very hypersexual things. I respect anybody who can, but it's terrifying to me. I don't know if that'll ever change. It's not like I only do wholesome things—my character literally gets gutted by Ghostface in Scream—but my dream is to try and be a Disney princess someday."

Grace is one of the many stars of Lionsgate's latest "Hunger Games" adaptation, pulling double duty as twins Maysilee and Merrilee Donner. The former is a tribute from Panem's District 12.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" hits theaters Nov. 20.

articles.title: Di Ferrero faz carinho em filhote de jumento durante visita ao PI | G1
articles.standfirst: Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, vocalista do NX Zero aparece dirigindo, encontra um grupo de animais e brinca com o filhote.
articles.summary: Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, vocalista do NX Zero aparece dirigindo, encontra um grupo de animais e brinca com o filhote.
articles.body:
O cantor Di Ferrero, vocalista da banda NX Zero, esteve no Piauí e publicou nas redes sociais um vídeo em que aparece fazendo carinho em um filhote de jumento. Durante o passeio, o artista avista o grupo de animais, interrompe o trajeto e se aproxima de um deles.

Na gravação, Di Ferrero conversa com o filhote e brinca com a possibilidade de levá-lo para casa. “Vamos morar lá em casa. Gostei de você. Você gostou de mim. Eu gostei de você” , diz o cantor enquanto faz carinho no animal.

Antes do encontro, o artista aparece parafraseando um trecho de uma música. Ao final do vídeo, ele se despede e deixa uma mensagem sobre o estado: “Bom dia. Bem-vindo ao Piauí, lugar mágico maravilhoso” .

A última passagem de Di Ferrero pelo estado havia ocorrido em novembro de 2023, quando o NX Zero participou do Festival GiraSol, realizado em Teresina nos dias 10 e 11 daquele mês.

articles.title: Jessé, grande cantor falecido há 33 anos em acidente de carro, é lembrado por Moisés Navarro no álbum 'Alguém cantando', mas falta foco ao repertório | G1
articles.body:
Jessé (1952 – 1993), cantor que entrou em cena há 50 anos com pseudônimo em inglês, é celebrado por Moisés Navarro no álbum 'Alguém cantando' — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Em 1974, o astro irlandês de origem argentina Chris de Burgh lançou canção, “Flying”, que ecoou no mundo todo e que, no Brasil, foi regravada em 1976, com a letra original em inglês, por um cantor brasileiro que adotou o pseudônimo de Christie Burgh.

Como a grafia similar dos nomes gerou ameaça de processo, esse cantor adotou ainda em 1976 outro pseudônimo, Tony Stevens, mantido até 1977. Nasceu ali, em 1976, há 50 anos, a carreira desse cantor brasileiro nascido em Niterói (RJ) e revelado em movimento do mercado fonográfico que, ao longo dos anos 1970, fez muitos cantores brasileiros adotarem pseudônimos em inglês para se passarem por astros norte-americanos.

O tal cantor, batizado Jessé Florentino Santos (25 de abril de 1952 –29 de março de 1993), seguiu a onda ao entrar em cena sem a verdadeira identidade, mas fez sucesso mesmo a partir de 1980 quando, após ter sido vocalista do grupo Placa Luminosa, adotou o prenome e se apresentou como Jessé no Festival MPB-80 (TV Globo), defendendo a música “Porto solidão” (1980), composta por Zeca Bahia a partir de versos do poeta Antonio Ginco, o Gincko.

Um dos maiores sucessos do festival, a canção “Porto solidão” alavancou a carreira de Jessé e, após 46 anos, reaparece na voz do cantor mineiro Moisés Navarro em dueto com Claudya, gravado por Navarro para “Alguém cantando”, álbum em que o artista aborda o repertório de Jessé.

Moisés Navarro canta músicas dissociadas da voz potente de Jessé (1952 – 1993) no álbum 'Alguém cantando', casos de 'A noite do meu bem', de 'Romaria' e da música-título de Caetano Veloso — Foto: Samuca Kim / Divulgação

Com lançamento programado para 13 de novembro, em edição da Companhia de Discos do Brasil, o álbum “Alguém cantando” joga luz sobre esse grande cantor fluminense falecido há 33 anos, a um mês de completar 41 anos, em decorrência de acidente de carro sofrido em estrada próxima da cidade Ourinhos (SP).

Gravado sob direção musical do pianista Alexandre Vianna, autor dos arranjos das 10 músicas, o álbum “Alguém cantando” foi batizado com o nome da composição de Caetano Veloso lançada pelo autor em 1977 no álbum “Bicho” e regravada por Jessé dez anos depois no álbum “Eterno menino” (1997).

A rigor, mais da metade do repertório do tributo de Moisés Navarro a Jessé é dissociada na memória popular da voz potente do cantor projetado no festival de 1980 – o que enfraquece a louvável iniciativa de Moisés Navarro.

São os casos das músicas “A noite do meu bem” (Dolores Duran, 1959), “Onde está você” (Oscar Castro Neves e Luvercy Fiorini, 1963), “Romaria” (Renato Teixeira, 1977) e “Irmãos da lua” (Renato Teixeira, 1982), cantadas por Jessé no show que gerou o álbum duplo ao vivo “O sorriso ao pé da escada” (1983), sendo que “Onde está você” também tinha sido gravada pelo cantor no ano anterior, no álbum intitulado “Jessé” (1982).

Já as músicas “Campo minado” (Mário Maranhão, Mário Marcos e Maximiliano) e “Voa, liberdade” (Mário Maranhão, Eunice Barbosa e Mário Marcos) foram efetivamente lançadas por Jessé em 1980 no primeiro álbum do cantor, gravado no embalo do sucesso de “Porto solidão” no festival MPB-80.

Música gravada por Moisés Navarro com a voz de Zeca Baleiro e a voz de Chico Lobo, “Solidão de amigos” (1982) também foi apresentada ao Brasil na voz do homenageado no já mencionado álbum “Jessé” de 1982.

Canção gravada por Jessé no derradeiro álbum do artista, “Raízes” (1992), “Paz do meu amor” (Luiz Vieira, 1963) completa o repertório desfocado do tributo “Alguém cantando”.

articles.title: Ingressos Festival de Parintins 2027: Veja preços e como comprar | G1
articles.standfirst: Pela primeira vez, a compra e o acesso ao Bumbódromo serão totalmente digitais. Não haverá emissão de ingressos físicos nem troca de vouchers nos escritórios da Amazon Best.
articles.summary: Garanta seu lugar no Festival de Parintins 2027: ingressos custam até R$ 4.800 e a venda para a edição de 60 anos será exclusivamente digital a partir de 28 de novembro.
articles.body:
Bumbódromo de Parintins — Foto: Divulgação/Secom

Os ingressos para o Festival Folclórico de Parintins 2027 começam a ser vendidos em 28 de novembro, às 9h (horário de Manaus ), exclusivamente pela internet . Os valores chegam a R$ 4.800 para o passaporte que dá acesso às três noites do evento. Confira os preços abaixo.

A venda será feita pela plataforma BaladAPP by Ticketmaster . Cada CPF poderá comprar até dois ingressos , por Pix ou cartão de crédito, com parcelamento em até três vezes sem juros.

Pela primeira vez, a compra e o acesso ao Bumbódromo serão totalmente digitais. Não haverá emissão de ingressos físicos nem troca de vouchers nos escritórios da Amazon Best.

A edição de 2027 será comemorativa pelos 60 anos do Festival e terá uma identidade visual especial, com o tema "Texturas de nossa infância", que acompanha a tradicional disputa entre os bois-bumbás Caprichoso e Garantido.

Os interessados devem criar uma conta na plataforma BaladAPP by Ticketmaster antes da abertura das vendas.

A partir das 9h de 28 de novembro, basta acessar o site da BaladAPP ( selecionar o Festival de Parintins 2027, escolher o setor e a modalidade de ingresso e concluir o pagamento.

A escolha do assento no mapa não garante reserva . O ingresso só estará confirmado após a aprovação do pagamento.

Não haverá venda por telefone, WhatsApp ou presencialmente nos escritórios da Amazon Best.

O público poderá escolher entre duas modalidades:

Passaporte: dá acesso às três noites do Festival, com um ingresso para cada apresentação.

Avulso: permite assistir a apenas uma noite, escolhida no momento da compra.

As duas modalidades estarão disponíveis nos quatro setores, com opções de inteira e meia-entrada.

Passaporte: R$ 4.800 (inteira) | R$ 2.400 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.600 (inteira) | R$ 800 (meia).

Passaporte: R$ 4.500 (inteira) | R$ 2.250 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.500 (inteira) | R$ 750 (meia).

Passaporte: R$ 3.960 (inteira) | R$ 1.980 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.320 (inteira) | R$ 660 (meia).

Passaporte: R$ 3.000 (inteira) | R$ 1.500 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.000 (inteira) | R$ 500 (meia).

Sobre o valor total da compra será cobrada uma taxa de processamento de 2%, informada antes da finalização do pagamento. Nenhum setor inclui serviço de open bar.

Os ingressos serão disponibilizados no aplicativo BaladAPP by Ticketmaster após a confirmação da compra. O QR Code será liberado 72 horas antes de cada noite de apresentação .

No dia do Festival, o público deverá abrir o ingresso no aplicativo e apresentar o QR Code junto com um documento oficial com foto.

Não serão aceitos ingressos impressos, capturas de tela ou fotografias do QR Code.

Como indicar outra pessoa para usar o ingresso

Quem comprar ingressos para outras pessoas deverá informar o nome de cada usuário na área "Meus Ingressos", no site da BaladAPP.

A pessoa indicada também precisa ter cadastro na plataforma, com o mesmo e-mail informado na indicação.

O prazo para indicar ou trocar o usuário termina às 16h do dia da apresentação. Será permitida apenas uma troca após a primeira indicação.

No caso do Passaporte, a indicação poderá ser feita separadamente para cada noite.

A meia-entrada será oferecida às categorias previstas na legislação, como estudantes, idosos a partir de 60 anos, jovens de baixa renda inscritos no ID Jovem, professores, profissionais da saúde, doadores regulares de sangue, órgãos e medula óssea e pessoas com deficiência, além de acompanhantes quando previsto em lei.

Para utilizar o benefício, será necessário apresentar documento oficial com foto e comprovante válido da condição que garante o desconto.

Os ingressos específicos para pessoas com deficiência (PCD) serão organizados pelo Governo do Amazonas e não estarão disponíveis na BaladAPP ou na Amazon Best.

As orientações podem ser obtidas pelos seguintes contatos:

Secretaria de Estado de Cultura e Economia Criativa (SEC-AM): (92) 3633-2850 e (92) 3633-3041.

Secretaria de Estado de Justiça, Direitos Humanos e Cidadania (Sejusc-AM): (92) 99324-5933.

O cancelamento poderá ser solicitado pela conta da BaladAPP em até sete dias após a compra, desde que o pedido seja feito com mais de 48 horas de antecedência da apresentação.

Para ingressos avulsos, será considerada a data do evento escolhido. No Passaporte, a referência será a primeira noite, em 25 de junho de 2027.

O prazo de reembolso é de até 72 horas para pagamentos por Pix e de 15 a 60 dias úteis para cartão de crédito. A taxa de processamento de 2% também será devolvida em caso de cancelamento integral da compra.

O não comparecimento ao evento não garante reembolso.

A Amazon Best terá pontos de atendimento em Manaus e Parintins para orientações sobre cadastro e indicação de usuários. Os escritórios não venderão ingressos nem farão reservas ou retiradas.

Manaus: Rua Nova Prata, 225, Nossa Senhora das Graças.

Parintins: Rua Vieira Junior, 754, Centro, em frente ao porto.

O atendimento da BaladAPP também pode ser feito pelo telefone (62) 3434-8450, pelo chat do site e aplicativo ou pelo e-mail contato@baladapp.com.br .

The Rajinikanth starrer added another Rs 95.55 crore net in its second week, taking its two-week domestic net collection to Rs 429.90 crore. With its India gross now nearing Rs 543 crore, the film is closing in on becoming the highest-grossing Tamil film of all time, with Vijay's 'LEO' (Rs 223 crore) record in Tamil Nadu also within reach.'Jailer 2' Live box office collectionAccording to Sacnilk, 'Jailer 2' has earned Rs 2.18 crore net in India on Day 21 so far from 6,891 shows. articles.title: Marc Maron is figuring out what to do with all his free time
articles.summary: After ending 'WTF With Marc Maron,' the comedian is embracing privacy, pursuing new projects and figuring out life beyond the microphone.
articles.body:
Marc Maron signed off of his podcast for the last time over a year ago the same way he always did.

It was an exclamation that paid tribute to his cat. His feline went missing after he moved to L.A. from New York. These days, Maron is still having conversations with his pets.

"Go back in the room, Buster," Maron tells his cat. Two of his furry roommates refuse to get along, forcing the comedian to alternate which one gets to roam freely around the house.

"It's my life," Maron said over Zoom, "but it's a pain in my a—."

Since ending his show, "WTF With Marc Maron," the comic has been rediscovering the mundane routines that make up a life.

"I do comedy every night, I exercise, I do work around the house, I've been reading a lot, trying to fill my head with stuff that makes me smarter somehow, or kind of makes me look at things differently," he said. "I tend to be pretty busy somehow, but I can make a day out of one or two errands."

After 16 years of booking guests, scheduling interviews and dissecting the existential dread of the current political climate, Maron suddenly has more free time than he's accustomed to, and needs to figure out what to do with it, a question he's exploring in a new special he's filming in December.

"We're considering calling the special 'Free Time,'" the comedian said.

Maron wasn't sure how ending his podcast would affect his comedic craft or his relationship with stand-up. It actually took him a few months to re-familiarize himself with being a comic.

"WTF" would start with a stream-of-consciousness monologue, and oftentimes those words translated into bits in his act. Without that thread of creativity, Maron is forced to have those conversations on stage instead of talking through them twice a week.

"I imagine that there was more stuff being generated on a week-to-week basis when I was thinking out loud, but that's OK," he said.

The change has also given Maron back his privacy. For 16 years, "WTF" served as a public diary. Across thousands of episodes, he processed relationships, grieved the loss of loved ones — including his creative collaborator and romantic partner Lynn Shelton, who died at 54 in May 2020 — and tried to make sense of his own anxieties.

"Now, without the constant conversations outside of just having conversations with my friends, a lot of the ideas develop on stage, and they don't start in public," he said. "It enables me to have some privacy over what I'm working on. And also over my life."

Maron also worried that ending the show might affect ticket sales. Instead, the newfound privacy has sparked curiosity among his audience.

"People genuinely kind of want to see what's going on with me because they were so used to hearing it every week," he said. "So it's sort of a big check-in."

Although Maron had spent years developing material through conversations in the garage, he wasn't sure how much that experience translated to acting.

"I do think that being in constant engagement with humans on the podcast or listening intently or empathetically is what acting is all about," Maron said. "But I certainly paid my dues in the garage."

Even with the extra time he finds himself with, Maron doesn't want to fully embrace the life of an actor and chooses not to take too much time away from the stage.

Going into filming Season 2 of the Apple TV series "Stick," which premieres Wednesday, he feared shooting would take place away from L.A.

"The greatest thing about this season was it was shot in L.A., as all things should be," Maron said.

Although acting doesn't offer the same creative freedom as comedy, Maron has grown more comfortable working within someone else's words. The experience allows him to draw from his own emotions while bringing another person's writing to life. In stand-up, his own experiences and choices drive the performance.

Maron's real-life relationship with golf isn't quite as involved as Mitts', the character he plays in the series. Asked about his own game, he quickly clarified that he doesn't play and has no plans to pick up the clubs. The sentiment can be seen through his character, an ex-caddy to a once promising star, Pryce Cahill (Owen Wilson) who is trying to coach an up-and-comer.

Still, learning to work within the emotional and physical boundaries of a script has helped him understand what fulfillment in acting can look like.

"I think that becoming more experienced with that and trying to work within those parameters to experience the fulfillment of what that particular craft offers," he said.

Working with Owen Wilson, Timothy Olyphant and Rhea Seehorn in Season 2 of "Stick" has also helped Maron appreciate the many approaches actors take to their performances. With more experience, he feels increasingly confident in his ability to access the emotional depth needed to embody somebody else's writing.

"I think that by working with other actors all the time, I'm kind of learning whatever my process is going to become," he said.

The extra time has also pushed Maron to challenge himself in new ways.

"We're kind of in the process of putting together a film that I plan to direct, maybe in the spring, hopefully, based on my good friend Sam Lipsyte's novel," Maron said.

But for now, he's going to continue living his real life and trying to figure out how to deal with living.

"Theoretically, we should be on the streets protesting every day, all day long, everybody," Maron said. "But, you know, I got things to do. I gotta buy potting soil, and, you know, plant a plant."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans, speaks out following the release of ‘You Can See Everything’
articles.summary: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, is sharing his thoughts on “You Can See Everything,” including what he believes is the biggest misconception about him and a slew of other topics.
articles.body: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, is sharing his thoughts on “You Can See Everything,” including what he believes is the biggest misconception about him and a slew of other topics. On Nov. 3, Evans invited people to participate in an AMA, ask me anything, on X, prefacing it needed “to be legally permisible (sic).” Among the lightest questions include someone asking what the first thing he and Holmes will do after she is released from prison. “Hold our kids tight and talk all night,” Evans, who shares two children with the Theranos founder replied. Holmes was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what her company’s technology could do. She was sentenced to 11 years in prison in 2022 and is currently at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas. “You Can See Everything,” the documentary by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, followed her and Evans weeks before she was incarcerated. The film has become a critical and commercial success, with many viewers and experts questioning her and Evans’ intentions. Fielder had previously shared during a Los Angeles screening in October that Evans had yet to watch the film ahead of its Oct. 16 release. When asked on X what he misses most about Holmes, Evans said “everything.” “I miss her presence. Her touch. The way she runs her fingers through my hair. Her patience. She makes me a better person. And without her, I feel an emptiness that’s hard to describe,” he wrote. “People often say they need someone when what they really mean is that they want them. I’ve thought a lot about that distinction. I need Liz. She should qualify as a medically necessary prescription.” When someone followed up by replying, “Her scrambled eggs,” Evans replied, “Def not this,” with a melting face emoji. In the documentary, there’s a moment when Holmes is whisking eggs in a yellow bowl. As she’s speaking to Fielder, Evans grabs the bowl from her hands and starts to vigorously whip them. When the filmmaker questions his move, Evans implies it’s because his partner doesn’t do it right. On X, Evans also shared he had seen “almost all of” Fielder’s work before filming “You Can See Everything.” He also wrote that they celebrated Fielder’s birthday “around the table in Del Mar with my family,” adding, “He also missed the Time 100 dinner, so we celebrated that too.” TODAY.com has reached out to Evans, Fielder and Holmes for additional comment. He also touched on more serious matters, including the “one misconception from the film” that he would like to dispel. “That I somehow control Liz. Anyone who actually knows her would find that idea hilarious. She’s fiercely independent, strong-willed, and my best friend,” he tweeted. “We are partners in every sense. We challenge each other, disagree, and face the world together. Her closest friends are also some of my closest friends. If I ever mistreated her, they’d have my head.” Someone also wondered why, in the documentary, he stopped Fielder from speaking to Holmes’ father. “Both Nathan and the audience saw it as integral to the documentary to truly ‘see everything,’” the person wrote. “It felt like a missed opportunity that could have continued to give Liz more light.” In his response, Evans noted that Holmes was going to prison and had three days together. “I wanted to spend that time together. He interviewed her parents after she went in. They chose not to include that in the film. I didn’t control the edit. If there was something the directors wanted from them they had multiple opportunities to get it.” When questioned about using his power of attorney over Holmes and going directly to X instead of her for her profile password, he wrote that they “discussed this at length over several months. She knew exactly what we were doing.” “We talk about everything, including X. Nothing happened behind her back,” he claimed. “The POA was simply the legal mechanism that allowed me to act on her behalf while she’s incarcerated. It was not a substitute for her consent.” When pressed for more clarity, he replied that Holmes’ account was “tied to an old Theranos email. Password forgotten.” “You Can See Everything” has continued to be a topic of conversation online. Whether the attention has been good or bad for Evans it’s unknown. However, when asked if he regretted agreeing to the documentary, he simply wrote, “Not at all.”

articles.body: Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor have been married for over 14 years, but their relationship attracted considerable attention even before they tied the knot in 2012. The couple had reportedly lived together for nearly five years before getting married, a decision that was considered unconventional at the time. Known as ‘Saifeena’, they often found themselves in the spotlight, with their choice to share a home before marriage becoming a talking point. Over the years, Kareena, Saif and their family members have spoken about how they reacted to the decision. While Kareena's family initially had reservations, Saif's mother, Sharmila Tagore, was particularly struck by the actress's candidness about their live-in relationship.In a 2019 conversation with Humans of Bombay, Kareena looked back at the time she spent with Saif on the sets of 'Tashan', where their relationship began. She spoke about how different they were and the influence he had on her. “He’s 10 years older than me and has two kids. But for me, he was just Saif. He helped me heal and love myself. Maybe it was the fact that we’re so different – he’s more private & not ‘Bollywoodised’, but I imbibed that from him. I learnt to balance things and not let them get to me,” she said.Kareena also recalled how Saif first suggested that they move in together. Having dated for some time, he felt they should spend more time together instead of continuing to drop her home every night. The actor subsequently spoke to Kareena's mother about their plans.“We’d been dating for a while, when he said he’s not 25 and can’t keep dropping me home every night. So he told my mom, ‘I want to spend the rest of my life with her. We want to live together.’ My mom was cool with it. It’s so easy with him. Even when we decided to get married, it felt right,” she recalled.However, the decision did invite some criticism, particularly because Kareena belonged to the illustrious Kapoor family. Her father, Randhir Kapoor, is the son of legendary filmmaker and actor Raj Kapoor, while her great-grandfather, Prithviraj Kapoor, was among the pioneers of Indian cinema. Her extended family includes actors Shashi Kapoor, Shammi Kapoor, Rishi Kapoor and Neetu Kapoor. Her mother Babita and sister Karisma Kapoor have also been part of the film industry, while cousin Ranbir Kapoor is among the leading actors of the current generation.In Gunjan Jain's book 'She Walks She Leads', Kareena spoke about why she decided to move out of her mother's home and share a house with Saif. She acknowledged that the decision surprised some people but maintained that she had nothing to hide.“Saif and I moved in together because I was ready to leave my mother’s house, and if he and I did not live together, we would barely meet. There were some raised eyebrows, especially since I am from the Kapoor khandaan. But I was always honest about it.”She also explained why she did not consider living together before marriage an issue, drawing a comparison with the way relationships are approached in the film industry. “In Bollywood, the tried-and-tested formula always works, so why not try and test a relationship? I didn’t see anything wrong in it.”Her sister Karisma Kapoor admitted that the decision had initially taken her by surprise as well. However, she eventually understood that Kareena was following her instincts and making a choice she believed was right.“It was for me too, to some extent. Our family is slightly conservative but then we accepted that this was Bebo: all heart and all sentiment. Besides, she has this incredible ability to always know what is right for her. She is led by emotion and instinct but, touch wood, her decisions have always proved to be positive and wise,” Karisma said.Karisma had previously shared screen space with Saif in films such as 'Hum Saath-Saath Hain', even before Kareena made her acting debut.Saif's mother, veteran actor Sharmila Tagore, had a rather different experience when she discovered that the couple were living together. During her appearance on 'Koffee with Karan' in 2023, she recalled a gathering at her Delhi home where Kareena casually spoke about her life with Saif in front of several guests.“I had friends over, lots of people from Delhi. These two came and were sitting there. I casually said, ‘What’s happening?’ and she (Kareena) said, ‘When Saif woke up in the morning, he told me this…’ giving the impression that they are living together. This is Delhi and these are my friends of my age,” she recalled.Sharmila, who had herself lived with Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi, fondly known as Tiger Pataudi, before marrying him in 1968, was amused by how openly Kareena spoke about their arrangement. Comparing the two generations, she said:“I was just thinking how the world has changed. When I was living with Tiger, when I was not married, I would not have said to a room full of people that I am living with him. It would have been a deep, dark secret. Maybe everyone would have known, but I wouldn’t have said it. But she said it so naturally that when I even think about it, I sort of laugh at how simple and sorted she is.”Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor got married in October 2012. They welcomed their first son, Taimur Ali Khan, in December 2016, while their younger son, Jeh Ali Khan, was born in February 2021.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Hailey Bieber Details Emotional Rollercoaster of PMDD Diagnosis After Son Jack Blues’ Birth: ‘Just a Really Intense and Special Journey’
articles.summary: The model and Rhode founder has talked before about the difficulty of premenstrual dysphoric disorder, a more severe form of premenstrual syndrome.
articles.body:
Hailey Bieber has been an open book when it comes to the joy of motherhood, but she has also been very frank about some of the challenges of raising son Jack Blues with husband Justin Bieber . In a new interview with Women's Wear Daily , the 29-year-old model and founder of Rhode cosmetics talked about her struggle with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a severe, hormonally driven mood disorder that is a more intense form of premenstrual syndrome.

"After I had my son, I struggled with [PMDD] a bit, and there's just not a lot of conversation or research around it," said Bieber.

According to Johns Hopkins Medicine , PMDD is a severe and chronic health condition whose symptoms start the week before menstruation and can include depressed mood and feelings of hopelessness, increased anxiety, mood swings, self-critical thoughts, sudden tearfulness, increased irritability and concentration problems, among others.

Bieber said that during her pregnancy and after Jack Blues' birth she experienced very intense emotional symptoms that made her realize that there is not enough conversation or research about a number of health issues women face.

"Especially after having my own child. That was just a really intense and special journey that I had," she said. "There's so much that happens when you are pregnant, during childbirth. There's so many things that happen leading up to having a child." Bieber said she kept having PMDD symptoms postpartum and after Jack's birth, "I struggled with that a bit, and there's just not a lot of conversation or research around it."

Bieber, who has spoken about her PMDD struggles before, said speaking in public about it makes her feel "less alone," and she hopes that it might lead to more open conversations among women in order to make it feel like "less of a lonely journey" for others. As a result of her experience, Rhode recently announced a $5 million, three-year partnership with the Foundation for Women's Health to support medical research, education and care in areas typically underfunded.

Hailey and Justin welcomed Jack in August 2024 and back in March she first opened up about her PMDD diagnosis on the SHE MD podcast, where she said she'd been diagnosed with the disorder six months after giving birth.

"I was like, 'This just feels way more intense than before,' like the lead-up to getting your period," she said in the previous interview of the emotional tumult she felt after Jack's birth, which she described as much different from the PMS she'd experienced before. "You're like, 'Why does it feel like my whole entire life is gonna end? Like, I don't understand.' You just have all these swirling thoughts and feelings, and just everything feels like the biggest deal in the world."

Bieber also explained that once her period began some of those more intense feelings began to recede and improve with time. In 2022, Beiber was hospitalized for a ministroke and then subsequently had a successful procedure to close a small hole in her heart .

articles.title: Actress Mckenna Grace rejects Hollywood nudity, 'hypersexual' roles
articles.summary: Mckenna Grace revealed she won't do nudity or hypersexual scenes in Hollywood, separately saying her ultimate dream is to become a Disney princess someday.
articles.body: Rising Hollywood star Mckenna Grace has drawn a firm line against participating in on-screen nudity, and separately revealed that her dream is to one day play a Disney princess. Speaking with Cosmopolitan, Grace explained that she respects actors who appear in explicit scenes but said those roles do not align with her personal career goals. "At this point, I definitely don’t do nudity or very hypersexual things," Grace said when asked whether there were any roles she would turn down. "I respect anybody who can, but it’s terrifying to me. I don’t know if that’ll ever change," she added. NATALIE PORTMAN SAYS BEING SEXUALIZED AS A CHILD STAR FORCED HER TO BECOME A 'GOOD GIRL' AS PROTECTION The 20-year-old actress, who is set to appear in the upcoming "Hunger Games" prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping," began acting as a child. Her credits include the "Ghostbusters" films, "Scream 7" and Hulu's "The Handmaid’s Tale," for which she earned an Emmy nomination. Grace said she does not intend to limit herself to wholesome roles. However, she hopes to pursue opportunities that align with her personal boundaries and long-term ambitions. "It’s not like I only do wholesome things — my character literally gets gutted by Ghostface in ‘Scream’ but my dream is to try and be a Disney princess someday," Grace added. On Tuesday, Grace clarified on Instagram that "The two quotes being used right now in these titles are unrelated," referring to her comments about wanting to play a Disney princess role. "I’m not uncomfortable doing nude scenes/hypersexual roles simply because ‘I want to be a Disney princess,’ it’s just because of my own personal comfortability I have with that sort of thing right now at this point in my life!" Grace added. DISNEY ALUM CHRISTY CARLSON ROMANO RIPS HOLLYWOOD FOR FAILING CHILD STARS AFTER HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S DEATH Grace is not alone in setting boundaries around intimate scenes in Hollywood. Entertainment critic Christian Toto suggested that Grace’s earlier appearances on family-friendly shows may have influenced her decision. "Mckenna got her showbiz start on family-friendly shows like ‘Crash & Bernstein.’ Perhaps some of those lessons have stuck," Toto, host of "The Hollywood in Toto Podcast," told Fox News Digital. "Or, she's seen former child stars go the hyper-sexual route and wants no part of it. Either way, her instincts here are solid, and she may just carve a healthy lane for her Hollywood career moving forward," he added. Actress Amy Adams previously recalled turning down a sexually explicit comedy sketch after portraying Giselle in Disney’s 2007 film "Enchanted." Speaking on "Late Night with Seth Meyers," Adams said she declined a graphic "Saturday Night Live" musical sketch proposed by Andy Samberg because she was mindful of the film's young audience. "I was so keenly aware of all the young girls that were watching ‘Enchanted,’" Adams said. "And I didn’t want to be the princess singing about that particular act, you know?" BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA Other actors have also established boundaries around intimate scenes. "You" star Penn Badgley discussed his request to reduce intimate scenes on his "Podcrushed" podcast in 2023, citing his marriage as a factor in the decision. Veteran actor Neal McDonough has also spoken publicly about his longstanding refusal to participate in sex scenes or kiss other actresses on screen, citing his Catholic faith and respect for his wife. Meanwhile, Angel Studios announced "The Angel Promise," a set of content standards that the Utah-based studio says will prohibit on-screen sex, nudity and gratuitous profanity in its original releases. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Angel Studios co-founder and chief content officer Jeff Harmon argued that Hollywood has increasingly moved away from the values of family audiences. "I think Hollywood generally kind of lives in a bubble," Harmon said. "These are excellent craftsmen. They're the best storytellers in the world. Hollywood has built the best storytelling infrastructure in the world." COMEDIAN LEANNE MORGAN CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD FOR LIVING IN A 'BUBBLE' AND MISJUDGING WHAT AUDIENCES WANT TO SEE "But at the same time, they've kind of drifted more and more away from the values-based audience that they used to serve," Harmon said. "And with that, in our view, as brothers and as fathers, as a father, Hollywood hasn't been giving me consistently what I need. Once in a while, you get a good one, but you have to sift through all these things to find your good movies and your good stories." Harmon said that the studio's pledge guarantees families will never have to worry about encountering graphic material, reflecting what he described as an audience-first model that aims to step out of the "Hollywood bubble" and into "middle America's shoes." articles.title: Actor assault case: HC reserves verdict on lawyer’s plea seeking contempt action against former judge
articles.summary: Kerala HC reserves verdict on lawyer TB Mini’s plea seeking suo motu contempt against former judge over alleged derogatory remarks in 2017 actor assault trial.
articles.body: Kochi: The high court on Wednesday reserved its judgment on a petition filed by T B Mini, the survivor’s counsel in the 2017 actor assault case, seeking suo motu contempt proceedings against former Ernakulam district judge Honey M Varghese for allegedly making derogatory remarks against her in open court during the trial.While considering the petition, Justice P V Kunhikrishnan orally questioned how the court could expunge remarks allegedly made by the trial court judge if they did not form part of the judicial record. The judge also observed that if the petitioner’s grievances concerned the media coverage, she could approach the Press Council of India.According to Mini, on Jan 12, 2026, the presiding officer of the trial court accused her, while she was representing the survivor, of attending the trial for fewer than 10 days, sleeping in court and treating the courtroom as a “resting place”. She alleged that the remarks, made in the presence of the media, were widely broadcast, triggering online abuse, character assassination and professional defamation against her.Mini had earlier approached the advocate general seeking sanction to initiate contempt proceedings. However, the request was rejected on April 22, 2026, with the observation that the judge’s remarks, even if true, amounted to “excessive or extravagant language” and did not meet the legal threshold for criminal contempt under the Contempt of Courts Act. Challenging the decision, Mini approached the HC, contending that the advocate general’s refusal to grant sanction did not curtail the high court’s inherent constitutional power to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.title: Wahlburgers Closes Last Standalone Restaurant in Boston After Worldwide Closures
articles.summary: Wahlburgers is saying goodbye to Boston — for now. The burger chain, owned by Mark Wahlberg and his brothers, Donnie Wahlberg and Paul Wahlberg, has closed n...
articles.body:
Wahlburgers is saying goodbye to Boston — for now.

The burger chain, owned by Mark Wahlberg and his brothers, Donnie Wahlberg and Paul Wahlberg , has closed nearly 80 locations since 2025 , USA Today reported, with its final standalone store closing in the company's home state: Massachusetts.

The burger chain took to Instagram on October 30 , announcing the closure of its last standalone store in Fenway Park in Boston, penning a hopeful message as Wahlburgers seeks a new home elsewhere in the city.

"Thank you, Fenway. 💚 After 11 years in the neighborhood, our Fenway location will close on October 31 as our lease comes to an end. We're grateful to everyone who joined us for game days, celebrations and everyday moments over the years. We're actively pursuing a new home in the Boston area and hope to have more to share soon," the post read, giving customers just one day's notice – similar to the announcement they made when closing their first-ever Massachusetts store .

But despite the Fenway closure, it's not the end for Wahlburgers. The company highlighted its 2026 wins and shared its plans for growth in the new year, despite seeing major closures across its worldwide restaurants.

"In 2026, we've added 10 new outlets to our portfolio and expanded partnerships across hospitality, retail and travel," the post continued. "And we're just getting started."

2027 will see Wahlburgers open in several new locations , the restaurant noted, including the Oakland Athletics' future Las Vegas stadium, The Orleans Hotel & Casino, Bass Pro Shops in California and Colorado, additional food stalls in various Home Depot locations and restaurants in Puerto Rico.

"Thank you for being part of our story, Fenway. We hope to see you before October 31, and we're excited for everything ahead," the post concluded.

As In Touch previously reported , the announcement came just one month after the original location of Wahlburgers said goodbye to loyal patrons.

The company's official Facebook page shared a message on September 29, announcing its sudden closure, revealing that the Hingham, Massachusetts, food joint would be shutting its doors the following day.

"Thank you for the memories," the statement began. "After nearly 15 years, our lease at the Hingham Shipyard is coming to an end and will close on Sept. 30."

"As the original Wahlburgers location, Hingham will always hold a special place in our story," the statement continued. "While this location is closing, we're actively looking for a new home in the Boston area and hope to have more to share soon."

Two other Boston locations of the Wahlburgers chain have shut down amid company closures over the last few years, NBC10 Boston reported , including its South Bay store in Dorchester and its MarketStreet location in Lynnfield.

articles.title: Danish students join European protest wave against education funding cuts
articles.summary: Danish government proposes scrapping allowance scheme for students from wealthier families.
articles.body:
Thousands of young people in Denmark have demonstrated against a government plan to cut student stipends under a decades-long allowance scheme, adding to a wave of youth unrest across Europe.

Organisers said up to 13,000 students marched from Copenhagen’s city hall square to parliament over proposed cuts to free up funds for defence spending on Monday, under the banner “Enough is Enough”.

The rally echoed student protests in France that spread to other European countries in recent weeks, and that morphed into wider grievances over the cost of living and housing crises impacting young people across the continent.

Student associations said some 40,000 students were on strike at 57 schools across Denmark over the proposed cuts.

Since 1970, all students enrolled in schools or university in Denmark over the age of 18 have automatically received the student allowance regardless of their parents’ income.

Students currently receive 1,154 kroner ($173) a month for those who live with their parents, and 7,426 kroner ($1,116) for those who live on their own.

Under the new government proposal, the allowance would be abolished for students living with parents earning over 700,000 Danish kroner ($105,248).

Only students living with parents earning between 419,589 kroner ($63,087) and 700,000 kroner ($105,248) a year would be eligible for the allowance, with stipends staggered based on their parents’ income.

Copenhagen police were out in force during the demonstration.

Thousands of young people chanted “Broken Promises” and carried signs reading “Save SU”, the Danish acronym for the student allowance, “Less Support, Less Educated” and “Don’t Cheat the Young”.

“In Denmark, we get funding and economic support for getting an education, and we’re very proud of this,” said one protest organiser, Danish High School Students Association president Oscar Tonsberg Hoffmann.

He told AFP that it would be wrong to dismantle “one of the world’s strongest educational systems”.

Kieran Hindshaw, a 23-year-old agronomy student, said he felt betrayed by the government.

“I’m infuriated that we finally get a supposedly ‘red’ government in Denmark that includes the left parties … we get cuts to our welfare and to the economies of young people whilst they’re funding corporate tax reductions and warfare,” he said.

The Higher Education Ministry said around 14,000 students are expected to lose their stipends, and some 8,000 would see it reduced.

The government has also proposed that unemployment benefits for recent university graduates be paid only to those who have worked during 18 of the last 24 months of their studies.

Industry Minister and Social Liberal Party leader Martin Lidegaard has meanwhile said the cuts “are not pleasant decisions”.

articles.title: Martha Stewart blames Craig Melvin for 'homeless' Halloween costume
articles.summary: Martha Stewart blames "Today" show host Craig Melvin for her "homeless" Halloween costume, which sparked backlash.
articles.body:
Martha Stewart isn't ready to accept blame for her Halloween costume that ruffled some feathers.

Stewart, 85, is blaming the "Today" show for the Halloween costume mishap that drew criticism from the public for mocking people experiencing homelessness.

Stewart's Halloween outfit sparked backlash ⁠ after she posted a since-deleted photo on Oct. 31 showing her in ripped jeans, a cream cardigan and a black knit cap, holding a sign that read, "I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!"

Stewart said "Today" show co-anchor Craig Melvin's chocolate spill is what lead to her outfit choice, according to comments she made on stage at the CrossCountry Mortgage Sales Rally in Orlando, Florida, on Nov. 3.

"He spilled chocolate all over my sweater, which I was going to wear on Halloween night," Stewart is heard saying in a video , shared by TMZ ⁠. "So when I picked up the sweater I said, 'Oh god it's so dirty and I only have 10 minutes to get dressed up for this Halloween party,' so the easiest costume was to get dressed up as bum."

The cookbook author was referring to her Oct. 30 appearance on the NBC's morning show , when Melvin, dressed as Snoop Dogg, accidentally spilled chocolate ganache while helping Stewart decorate a cheesecake.

"Real Snoop would never do that," Stewart joked on the morning show.

At the Tuesday event, Stewart recalled what happened next: "I looked at myself. I said, 'You really look hungry and homeless.' So I wrote a sign that said 'I'm hungry,' and boy, did that go off."

Critics accused her of making light of homelessness. In an initial Nov. 1 statement to People magazine, Stewart said the costume was meant to "bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness" and cited her support for charities working on the issue.

See Martha Stewart through the years, from recipes to the red carpet

"It's hard to admit when you've really screwed up," she wrote. "I know many people are suffering economically. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I am very sorry."

Stewart was among several celebrities whose Halloween looks drew criticism this year.

See the stars on Halloween as spooky season takes over Hollywood

Jessica Alba deleted photos of her Nancy Kerrigan costume ⁠, which included a knee bandage with fake blood, after commenters objected to its reference to the 1994 attack on the figure skater.

Paris Hilton also defended her family's "Beauty and the Beast" costumes ⁠ after followers questioned why she dressed as Belle while daughter London went as Chip, explaining that her daughter had chosen the teacup character.

articles.title: Ángel Martín: "El pasado es una herramienta muy útil para torturarte"
articles.standfirst: El humorista atiende a Tiramillas para hablar sobre su debut en la ficción con la novela 'El día que lo fuimos todo'
articles.summary: El humorista atiende a Tiramillas para hablar sobre su debut en la ficción con la novela 'El día que lo fuimos todo'
articles.body: Hay conversaciones que empiezan mucho antes de que se formule la primera pregunta. Tiramillas, la web de ocio de Marca, acude al hotel boutique Petit Palace Lealtad Plaza, en pleno corazón de Madrid, acude a la cita con Ángel Martín, uno de los humoristas más reconocibles de nuestro país, para hablar de su primera novela, 'El día que lo fuimos todo' (Planeta), una historia que, entre el humor y la emoción, invita a detenerse en los recuerdos, las decisiones que marcan nuestro camino y todo aquello que, por mucho que nos empeñemos, escapa a nuestro control. Desde sus comienzos en el 'stand-up' hasta su popularidad televisiva en 'Sé lo que hicisteis', pasando por sus virales 'Informativos matinales para ahorrar tiempo', Ángel Martín ha construido una trayectoria en la que el humor convive con una mirada especialmente lúcida sobre las contradicciones humanas. En 2021, con 'Por si las voces vuelven', compartió su experiencia tras sufrir un brote psicótico y convirtió un relato íntimo en un fenómeno editorial. Dos años después, en 'Detrás del ruido', profundizó en el proceso de reconstrucción personal. Ahora cambia de registro y se adentra por primera vez en la ficción. El protagonista de 'El día que lo fuimos todo' es Abel, un hombre solitario, algo apagasueños y poco amigo de las complicaciones, que emprende un trayecto en tren que terminará alterando su vida. Durante ese viaje, aparentemente cotidiano, se cruzan recuerdos, encuentros inesperados, situaciones ridículas y reflexiones sobre la pérdida, la amistad y el amor. Ángel Martín utiliza ese espacio cerrado y ese tiempo limitado para construir una historia en la que el humor no resta profundidad a las emociones, sino que convive con ellas. Con la libertad que ofrece la ficción, el autor explora también nuestras contradicciones, la tendencia a idealizar lo que dejamos atrás y esa necesidad, a veces agotadora, de intentar tenerlo todo bajo control. Porque quizá una de las grandes lecciones de la novela sea que no somos tan distintos como pensamos y que, incluso en los momentos en los que solo queremos que nos dejen tranquilos, hay algo que nos une a los demás. De todo ello, y de lo que supone pasar de contar la propia historia a inventar la de otro, hablamos con Ángel Martín. PREGUNTA. Después de hablar de experiencias personales en 'Por si las voces vuelven' y 'Detrás del ruido', ¿qué te lleva ahora a contar una historia de ficción y a esconderte detrás de un personaje como Abel? RESPUESTA. Pues me apetecía mucho experimentar con la novela. Creo que es una de las cosas que todavía no había hecho en comedia. Siempre había estado haciendo ficción con los monólogos, en 'Siete vidas', en 'Sé lo que hicisteis'... Siempre había escrito ficción, pero nunca me había planteado la posibilidad de que algunas historias encajaran mejor en una novela que en cualquier otro formato. Suelo escribir por las noches, a ratos, cosas que me divierten, que me entretienen, sin ningún rumbo. Sin embargo, un día, revisando todo el material que tenía escrito, pensé: "Espera, aquí hay una idea común, aquí está pasando algo que me estoy perdiendo". Entonces empecé a unir todas las ideas que tenía y me di cuenta de que aquello podía ser una novela, de que podía salir una novela de ahí. Llamé a mi editora y le eché un vistazo a lo que tenía, por si acaso era una locura y me decía: "No, aquí no hay nada". Pero me dijo que creía que había una novela. Así que empecé a trabajar en ello. Lo hice por esa sensación de querer experimentar ya con ese tipo de ficción. Tenía muchas ganas, sobre todo, de poder meter a un personaje que no fuera yo en jardines que no tuviera que resolver yo. P. Abel es un hombre solitario, un tanto apagasueños y aparentemente empeñado en que nadie le moleste demasiado. ¿Qué parte de Ángel Martín hay en él y qué parte has necesitado inventar? R. Hay mucho de mí. Abel no es Ángel Martín con otro nombre, por así decirlo, pero una de las cosas que me propuse al escribir 'El día que lo fuimos todo' era que, al ser la primera vez que me embarcaba en algo así, no quería experimentar demasiado intentando hacer algo que no tuviera nada que ver conmigo y en lo que no se reconociera nada mío. Corría el riesgo de que no se entendiera la novela, porque no tengo las herramientas ni la experiencia necesarias para dibujar algo que no conozco. Cuando intentas escribir para provocar emociones en quien te lee, decides: "Aquí quiero que sientas esto; aquí, esto otro". Para encontrar esas emociones, trataba de buscarlas en mí. Había muchas cosas que tú has pensado, vivido o sentido, que te suenan o que te han contado, que has leído o visto. La base estaba ahí. Lo que pasa es que, a la hora de escribirlo, me decía: "Bueno, ahora no voy a contar lo que pensaría yo ni lo que haría yo. Vamos a hacer que Abel haga otra cosa y a ver por dónde sale". Pero, al menos, eso me permitía crear un personaje coherente. Si empiezas a inventártelo todo, corres el riesgo de que, de repente, nada encaje. Sería como decir: "Bueno, tío, por eso no se entiende nada y por eso todo es un puto desastre". Creo que utilizarte a ti mismo como referencia, ir sacando cositas de aquí, ponerlas allí, quitar esto, incorporar algo que has visto o algo que te haría gracia que el personaje tuviera hace que, inevitablemente, como la base está muy centrada en cosas que tú puedes pensar, vivir o sentir, resulte reconocible. Pero yo no soy tan amargado como puede parecer Abel en ocasiones. Estoy lejos de serlo, pero me apetecía amargarlo un poco. P. La novela transcurre durante un trayecto de tren que termina cambiando para siempre la vida del protagonista. ¿Qué tiene un viaje en tren que lo convierte en un escenario tan adecuado para hablar de la vida, de las decisiones y de esos momentos que nos cambian? R. Sobre todo, me permitía controlar el espacio y el tiempo. No te voy a engañar: cuando pensaba en escribir una novela, me daba mucho miedo embarcarme en algo que, de repente, fuera el día uno, el día dos, una semana después, un mes después... porque eso me iba a obligar a tener unos conocimientos sobre cómo escribir una novela que todavía no tengo. No quería embarcarme en tener una pizarra llena de pósits, esquemas y no sé qué, porque pensaba: "Es que me voy a hacer la picha un lío en el capítulo dos". Así que meter a alguien en un tren y establecer una especie de cuenta atrás, con la obligación de llegar a un sitio en un tiempo determinado, era el espacio ideal. Sabes que no tienes que guardar demasiada información sobre lo que ha pasado, porque sabes dónde estás y el tiempo transcurre en tiempo real. No hay más. Además, es un lugar donde no conoces a nadie. Yo creo que no hay un lugar más solitario que un tren, en realidad. Aunque estés rodeado de gente y te puedan pasar millones de cosas, como tampoco me atrevía mucho a crear una novela con muchísimos personajes y muchas conversaciones, aquello era un poco peligroso para mí. Sin embargo, la herramienta del monólogo se me da bien. Sí podía crear conversaciones y un personaje que estuviera muy pendiente de lo que sucede en su cabeza, de cómo son sus pensamientos. A Abel le pasa muchas veces que está lo que quiere decir, lo que le gustaría decir, lo que realmente dice y lo que piensa en relación con eso que ha dicho. Y todo eso le lleva a preguntarse: "¿Por qué soy yo así? A lo mejor es por esto...". Esas capas que me permitían entrar en la cabeza del personaje me parecían ideales en un tren, porque es un sitio donde puedes estar solo de forma creíble. Puedes dejar solo a quien quieras en cualquier lugar: encerrado en un hotel porque se han ido todos de vacaciones y él se ha quedado ahí. Pero, hostia, ¡es que te puedes meter en un tren y ya está! Vas a estar solo. No pasa nada. P. En el libro conviven el humor y temas como la pérdida, el amor o la amistad. ¿Dónde está para ti la frontera entre hacer reír y abordar aquello que nos duele? R. No creo que haya una frontera clara. Creo que la marca quien recibe la broma o el tema del que estás hablando. Yo no puedo saber cuál es tu límite respecto al humor o al drama. No te conozco tanto. Puedo saber cuál es el mío, cuánto tolero el humor, cuándo una broma me hace daño, me ofende o no... Eso sí puedo saberlo de mí, pero no de los demás. Por eso, cuando me embarco en un proyecto, trato de medir muy bien la profundidad de las cosas en función de lo que es y de la intención que tiene. Pero no creo que exista un límite claro que determine dónde está la frontera. Tú puedes coger algo y decir: "¡Hostia, qué risa!", y otra persona puede verlo y pensar: "Bueno, es indignante que hayas publicado esto". Y yo qué sé... Pues no lo sé. A esa persona le ha parecido bien. Siéntate con ella y habla. ¿Qué quieres que te diga? Es algo muy individual. La comedia es muy, muy individual. Y cuando te dedicas al humor, sabes perfectamente cuándo estás haciendo comedia y cuándo has cruzado la línea. Lo sabes perfectamente. P. En 'Por si las voces vuelven' hablaste de tu propia experiencia con una enorme honestidad. En esta novela, en cambio, puedes refugiarte en la ficción. ¿La ficción permite decir algunas cosas que resultaría más difícil confesar en primera persona? R. Supongo que dependerá del atrevimiento de cada uno. Yo creo que la ficción te permite incluso explorar cosas que tú no piensas, para ver cómo te sientes ante ese pensamiento. Eso es lo divertido. Puedes decir: "Ni de broma pienso lo que piensa este tipo, pero es más divertido que piense esto, porque va a meterlo en este jardín o va a hacer que tenga que pasar por este proceso". Creo que son mundos muy distintos, muy, muy distintos. Por eso, tratar de comparar ficción y realidad me parece absurdo. Cuando alguien se ofende porque en una ficción un personaje dice o hace algo indignante, me pregunto: "¿Pero qué es lo que te ofende? No entiendo qué te ofende. ¡Es que no existe!". Quiero decir, es un personaje en un mundo de ficción. No está pasando nada. No le ha hecho daño a nadie. Son unas palabras y una imagen que tú te has montado en la cabeza. Hay una diferencia enorme. Es verdad que con la ficción puedes jugar un poco. Sabes que hay ciertos momentos en los que puedes decir: "Bueno, pues esto lo voy a poner así porque sé que te va a provocar un poquito, según cómo seas, y me divierte provocarte un poco". Porque, al final, te puedes enfadar mucho, pero... ¡ni que me cuentas! Si el chalado este ha dicho eso, ¿yo qué voy a hacer? No sé, es un personaje. Pero creo que tiene que ver también con lo que hablábamos antes, con los límites de cada uno. Es que hay quien piensa que en la ficción ni siquiera se debería poder decir determinadas cosas, y yo creo que está precisamente para ser todo lo extravagante que quieras y más, porque es ficción. El problema lo tiene quien no sepa distinguir la realidad de la ficción. Pero, claro, ahí no voy a entrar a educar. P. El título, 'El día que lo fuimos todo', habla de un pasado que parece tener un peso enorme. ¿Somos demasiado propensos a idealizar aquello que fuimos o que creemos haber perdido? R. Creo que somos propensos a compararnos cuando estamos mal. Cuando estamos mal, tendemos a decir: "Es que antes estaba mejor". Porque, cuando estamos bien, no solemos mirar atrás y pensar: "No, es que antes estaba peor". Eso no lo hacemos tanto. Nos gusta pensar que todas las cosas que no decidimos o que no hicimos eran, en realidad, las que habría sido más inteligente hacer, las que tendríamos que haber elegido. Pero no lo sabes. Estás fantaseando sobre lo que habría pasado si hubieras hecho o dicho otra cosa. Creo que el pasado es una herramienta muy útil para torturarte de forma fantasma. Es como cuando dices: "Si no hubiera dejado aquel trabajo, ahora estaría mejor. Yo lo sé, estaría mejor". Pero ¿por qué lo dejaste? "Porque estaba mal". Pues entonces no estarías mejor. Quiero decir, aquello no iba a mejorar. A veces necesitas que alguien venga y, cuando dices: "No, es que lo que tendría que haber hecho era esto", te recuerde: "Vamos a recordar por qué tomaste aquella decisión, a ver si estás tan seguro de esta mierda". Pero tendemos a idealizar todo lo que no pasó. P. Abel se enfrenta a planes que no salen como esperaba y a decisiones cuyas consecuencias escapan a su control. ¿Cuánto nos cuesta aceptar que, por mucho que intentemos organizar nuestra vida, hay cosas que sencillamente no dependen de nosotros? R. Yo creo que nos cuesta mucho, pero es que más te vale rendirte, porque no vas a poder controlarlo todo. Puedes diseñar un plan sobre cómo te gustaría que sucedieran las cosas, incluso escribirlo en un papel y hacer una pizarra con todo organizado, pero luego la realidad tiene otros planes. Quiero decir, tú puedes venir aquí a grabar esta conversación y que la cámara decida que no funciona. Lo tenías todo súper previsto, súper organizado, pero la cámara no va. No hay más. O puedes venir a hablar conmigo y que yo te diga: "Pues me encuentro mal y me tengo que ir a casa". No puedes prever lo que va a pasar con los demás. Lo único que puedes prever es lo que vas a hacer tú ante las cosas y cómo vas a reaccionar cuando sucedan. Pero tratar de controlarlo todo es estúpido. Creo que hay una edad en la que nos esforzamos por controlarlo todo, pero todavía somos bobos y no sabemos que es imposible. Después llega un día en el que te haces adulto y dices: "No, no, esto consiste en gestionar lo que va pasando lo mejor posible para que no se convierta en un infierno". Y ya está. P. En la novela también hay momentos en los que los personajes simplemente hacen el ridículo. ¿Crees que el humor nace muchas veces de nuestra incapacidad para controlar la imagen que queremos proyectar ante los demás? R. Yo creo que sí. Es muy divertido. De hecho, es una de las cosas maravillosas que tiene el humor: ver a alguien intentando ser quien no es. Es de las cosas que más gracia hacen. Ver a alguien fingiendo ser una persona que no es, porque, además, está fingiendo y va a tener que comportarse como alguien que no es. Hay pocas cosas más graciosas que ver a un amigo tuyo, que es un inseguro, haciéndose el chulo delante de la chica a la que quiere gustarle. Porque piensas: "Ojalá le diga que sí, porque este tío no aguanta el personaje ni media hora. Como la chica le diga de ir a tomar algo, es que este se nos hunde. No va a soportarlo". Fingir que eres algo que no eres es maravilloso, da mucha comedia. La vergüenza ajena da mucha comedia. P. Has construido buena parte de tu carrera alrededor del humor, pero también has demostrado que puedes hablar de asuntos muy difíciles sin perderlo. ¿Qué has descubierto sobre ti mismo al escribir una novela en la que el humor ya no depende de un escenario, sino de la historia y de sus personajes? R. Que no voy a estar contigo mientras la lees. A diferencia de lo que ocurre con los monólogos, en los que estoy contigo mientras me escuchas, aquí no estoy presente. En un monólogo puedes medir muy bien los tiempos e intuir el ambiente de la sala. Sabes si puedes retrasar una broma, si tienes que subir o bajar el volumen, dónde puedes mirar para que la broma funcione mejor, si un gesto o un silencio pueden cambiar las cosas... Estás construyendo con el público, en tiempo real, la emoción que quieres provocar. Con una novela escribes con la esperanza de que quien la coja sepa interpretar las palabras desde el lugar al que tú quieres llevarlo. Por eso requiere mucha más disciplina a la hora de elegir las palabras y manejar los tiempos. Si hay un momento en el que quiero que sientas cierta lástima por una situación, no sé en qué estado de ánimo vas a encontrarte cuando llegues a él. A lo mejor estás en un momento especialmente sensible y te llega mucho más rápido, pero quizá estás eufórico y ese momento no te provoca nada. Creo que lo más complicado de escribir una novela es intentar construir las emociones que quieres que experimente el lector, independientemente del estado de ánimo en el que se encuentre. Cruzas los dedos y piensas: "Necesito que, cuando lo cojas, lo hagas desde este estado de ánimo". No sé cómo vas a estar, pero voy a intentar que, cuando empieces a leer, pienses: "Mira este tío, menudo gilipollas. Está esperando el tren y no para de...". Que tenga ahí un jardín, que se le acerque una tía y le pregunte qué ha dicho y él piense: "¡Hostia, déjame en paz!". Necesito que sea un tipo que transmita esa sensación de "déjame en paz", porque creo que, independientemente de cómo estés, vas a poder conectar con él. Todos nos hemos sentido alguna vez así: "Hostia, hoy no me molestéis, dejadme en paz". Y, a partir de ahí, empiezas a construir: "Vale, si consigo que te sientas como este personaje, vamos a ver si podemos llevarte a otros sitios". Escribir una novela es un poco más frágil, más delicado. Requiere más paciencia y tiempo. P. Si 'Por si las voces vuelven' y 'Detrás del ruido' hablaban en buena medida de cómo reconstruirse después de tocar fondo, ¿qué crees que cuenta 'El día que lo fuimos todo' sobre lo que hacemos con nuestra vida cuando ya no podemos volver atrás? R. Yo creo que habla de cuánto nos cambia, sin darnos cuenta, descubrir que alguien cercano está a punto de morir. Es algo inevitable. Cuando recibimos una noticia así, creo que hacemos una especie de balance. No solo de la relación que tenemos con esa persona, sino también de nuestra propia vida. Muchas veces nos ponemos en el lugar del otro. No sé si a ti te sucede, pero generalmente pensamos: "Hostia, esto podría ser yo. Me podría haber pasado a mí, me podría pasar mañana. Podría haber sido yo". Y eso, inevitablemente, te lleva a hacer una especie de balance y a mirarte a ti mismo para preguntarte en qué punto estás y si realmente quieres seguir por ese camino, si tienen sentido algunas de las cosas que estás haciendo. Creo que El día que lo fuimos todo tiene un poco que ver con eso: con preguntarte cuánto de lo que eres te gusta, cuánto sentido y valor tienen lo que haces, lo que tienes y las cosas por las que estás luchando; cuántas cosas no estás atendiendo y quizá deberías prestarles un poco más de atención. Creo que va un poco por ahí: por pararnos a pensar en nosotros mismos, en por qué estamos donde estamos. A lo mejor estás librando batallas que ahora mismo no tiene sentido librar y necesitas tener otras peleas en otro sitio. P. Después de haber escrito sobre experiencias que forman parte de tu propia vida y ahora haber creado una historia completamente de ficción, ¿qué te gustaría que un lector se llevara consigo cuando cierre 'El día que lo fuimos todo'? R. Que somos más amigos de lo que creemos. Yo creo que, cuando escribo, lo que pretendo transmitir es esa sensación. 'Por si las voces vuelven' y 'Detrás del ruido' tenían una intención mucho más clara, iban directos a un sitio muy concreto, pero creo que detrás de todas las novelas hay una especie de mensaje: "No eres tan raro. No te preocupes tanto por si estás desencajando, por si las cosas no son como deberían ser. Relájate, porque todos somos bastante más parecidos de lo que crees. Todos pasamos por situaciones muy similares y pensamos y nos preocupamos por cosas muy parecidas". Cuando leo un libro y de repente me identifico con algo, siento una pequeña sensación de alivio: "Hostia, mira, este personaje me entiende". Aunque, en realidad, no es que me entienda el personaje, sino que me entiende la persona que ha escrito ese personaje y que se ha molestado en entenderme. Así que, si termina de leer esta novela con la sensación de que somos un poco más amigos, yo me doy con un canto en los dientes. Si además se ha reído, ya es como para alegrarme infinitamente. Y si también se ha emocionado un poco, entonces me alegro el triple.

articles.title: AMC has “recovered,” says CEO Adam Aron.

articles.title: Salman Khan's house firing: Shooter denied bail for brother's wedding, court says can attend it virtually
articles.summary: A special court here on Wednesday denied temporary bail to alleged shooter Vickykumar Gupta, arrested in the 2024 firing outside actor Salman Khan's
articles.body: A special court here on Wednesday denied temporary bail to alleged shooter Vickykumar Gupta, arrested in the 2024 firing outside actor Salman Khan's residence, to attend his brother's wedding in Bihar, but allowed him to join in the ceremony via video conference from jail.Gupta, along with co-accused Sagar Pal, had carried out the firing outside Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartment on April 14, 2024 morning.Salman Khan's house shooter seeks temporary releaseIn a plea filed before a special MCOCA court judge S Navander, Gupta had sought temporary release on December 1 and 2, 2026, to attend the marriage of his biological brother in Bihar's West Champaran district.Court orders accused to attend brother's wedding virtuallyThe court turned down the plea for his release.It, however, directed the jail authorities to make necessary arrangements for Gupta to attend the wedding ceremony through video conferencing subject to technical feasibility and prison security requirements."The video-conferencing arrangement shall be conducted under the supervision of the jail authorities, in accordance with applicable jail rules and security protocols. It shall not entail the applicant's release from custody," the court said in its order.The judge directed Gupta to provide an email ID to facilitate the virtual link.About the shooting caseGupta, Pal and three other accused are facing trial for offences registered under IPC provisions for criminal conspiracy, attempt to murder and relevant provisions of the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, (MCOCA).Bollywood stars face series of threatsMeanwhile, in Bollywood, several actors over the past months have taken the legal route over death threats and extortion calls, allegedly from members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. After the unfortunate firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff, IANS reported that Bollywood actor Ayushmann Khurrana had also received a threatening audio clip. The person claimed to be part of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang and reportedly demanded crores of rupees. Meanwhile, the cyber cell is also reportedly tracing the number and location from which the message was sent to Ayushmann.The Bishnoi group also claimed responsibility for the attack on Tiger Shroff, which took place on October 18 this year.Anil Pandit, a representative of the group, shared a social media post saying that they will not spare anyone working in close proximity with Salman Khan. He even released an audio clip, saying, "Listen to me carefully Salman Khan. If you don't apologize to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won't even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind. Don't think that you are in security and nothing will happen to you." he said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'Ramayana' eyes Rs 75-100 crore opening at Indian box office; Ranbir Kapoor and Yash starrer has potential to hit Rs 2,500 to 3,000 crore: Experts
articles.summary: With its epic scale, a star-studded cast and a story rooted in India's cultural consciousness, \"Ramayana\" is expected to open to bring Rs 75-100 crore on
articles.body: With its epic scale, a star-studded cast and a story rooted in India's cultural consciousness, "Ramayana" is expected to open to bring Rs 75-100 crore on its opening day across languages with experts projecting lifetime collections of Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 3,000 crore if it resonates with audiences.The grand cinematic adaptation of one of the most enduring epics in India will make its debut in theatres on Thursday. It stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana.Prominent film exhibitor Vishek Chauhan said "Ramayana" cannot be judged by conventional film review standards because a section of the audience will approach it through devotion and reverence."You cannot call "Ramayana" a classic film like 'Dhurandhar', 'Border' or 'Baahubali', this is a different genre of filmmaking. This is about religion, it is faith-based cinema."It is about the biggest deity in this country, Lord Ram... a huge audience will watch it as a piece of faith. If that faith connects, then there's no stopping for this film. It is a review and critic-proof film (in that sense)," the exhibitor told PTI.Chauhan, who is the owner of Roopbani Cinema in Bihar's Purnia, cited the success of recent faith-centric films like "Hanuman Ansh", "Karuppu", and "Irumudi", to highlight how religious sentiment can lead to unusual theatrical turnout."If a Rs 2-crore film on Neem Karoli Baba can do Rs 300-350 crore in India, then you are talking about the greatest religious tale ever told in this country. If it connects with the Hindu devotee base, 'Ramayana' has the potential to do Rs 2,500 to 3,000 crore," he said.Veteran distributor and exhibitor Raj Bansal said "Ramayana" could surpass the box-office collections of "Dhurandhar" franchise, which reportedly stands at over Rs. 3,000 crore."'Ramayana' can become India's biggest cinematic film. Most importantly, Diwali is celebrated because of Lord Rama and here we're coming up with a film on him," Bansal, who is the director of the Entertainment Paradise, a multiplex in Jaipur, told PTI.Exhibitor Akshaye Rathi said the film has the potential to set new box-office benchmarks, given its cast, technical brilliance and its scale."'Ramayana' is a story that resonates with every Indian, we all have grown up listening to this story and have deep emotional connection to it... If the storytelling finds resonance, then it will break every glass ceiling and set a new benchmark," Rathi, who owns multiple cinema theatres across central and western Indian markets operating across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh, told PTI.Sameer Munshi, chief operating officer of Miraj Entertainment Ltd, believes the Rs 1,000 crore milestone is within the film's reach, and said it can open at Rs 75-80 crore nett or Rs 100 crore (gross) across languages in India."'Ramayana' is a story that belongs to every Indian household, and it has the potential to be one of the biggest theatrical successes in Indian cinema. We expect the opening weekend through Diwali to be on par with, or ahead of, the biggest openers we have seen. This is also a film that will keep growing over weeks as families and repeat audiences come in through the festive and holiday season," Munshi told PTI.Ashish Misra, head of commercialisation at Cinepolis India, said the chain had sold more than one lakh tickets for the film and planned over 1,600 shows on opening day.He cautioned against judging the film's prospects solely through its first-day collections as its release coincides with Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations."One thing to keep in mind is the calendar. Friday is Dhanteras, Saturday is Choti Diwali and Sunday is Diwali, so until Sunday we could see some impact on collections from the festival celebrations, with families at home for the puja or out with relatives, especially for the evening shows. Monday is when the week properly begins," Misra told PTI.According to Munshi, demand at Miraj cinemas is particularly strong in Delhi-NCR, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, while Tier-2 markets are tracking ahead of expectations.The company plans to screen the film across 225 screens, with 960 shows a day, offering it in Hindi, Kannada, Telugu and Tamil."There is no blanket price hike, especially in the Southern states. Most screens are at regular festive rates, and in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns we are keeping pricing family-friendly. We've also created special festive food and beverage offerings to make the outing memorable," Munshi said.Rathi pointed out that advance bookings were showing greater traction in premium formats such as IMAX and 3D."While IMAX tickets are priced at Rs 3,000 and above or a little less, the average ticket price is lower, it is starting from Rs. 200, which is reasonable price for a Diwali bonanza of this scale and ambition. Also, the pricing will be different in different cities," he said.The film's prospects in the southern markets, however, appear measured due to the release of regional films like Suriya's "Scene" and Nayanthara's "Mookuthi Amman 2".Chennai-based trade expert Ramesh Bala said the buzz for "Ramayana" is stronger in Karnataka, where Yash enjoys popularity, while Pallavi's presence could attract audiences in other southern states.He expects "Ramayana" to earn around Rs 30 to 40 crore from the South market, and said the film relies heavily on word of mouth."The curiosity is more about the two South films and there's moderate buzz in the South about 'Ramayana'. It is not like other Pan-Indian movies.
